goal: The per-store document, books and sync jobs find due work through an index or a mark and look at an idle store at most hourly: an invoice tick, an email check and an e-invoice check read fewer than 100 rows of orders and invoices in a store with 2,000 invoiced orders, every book gets its turn, and an idle tick reads no page, product, variant, order or media row.

commits.title: Indexes that fit the document jobs' windows

changes.how: Custom migration: `pnpm exec drizzle-kit generate --custom --name document_job_indexes`, then `node scripts/prune-snapshots.mjs`. Eight plain `create index if not exists` statements; none of these tables is on the hot list (orders, order_lines, visits, products, product_variants, customers, carts, cart_lines), so no `concurrently`: (1) invoices_issued_at_idx on commerce.invoices (issued_at); (2) credit_notes_issued_at_idx on commerce.credit_notes (issued_at); (3) invoices_business_issued_idx on commerce.invoices (issued_on) where (snapshot -> 'buyer' ->> 'type') = 'business'; (4) credit_notes_business_issued_idx, the same on commerce.credit_notes; (5) work_invoices_business_issued_idx on commerce.work_invoices (issued_on) where status <> 'draft' and not imported and (buyer ->> 'business')::boolean is true; (6) work_credit_notes_business_issued_idx on commerce.work_credit_notes (issued_on) where (buyer ->> 'business')::boolean is true; (7) order_events_invoice_failed_idx on commerce.order_events (created_at) where type = 'invoice.failed'; (8) order_edits_documents_waiting_idx on commerce.order_edits (store_id) where status = 'applied' and documents = 'waiting'. Write each predicate with exactly the expression the reading statement uses (src/server/einvoice-sending.ts lines 64 to 93, src/server/invoice-notices.ts lines 131 to 162), or Postgres will not match the partial index. Mirror all eight in src/db/schema.ts on their tables so `pnpm db:check` agrees (drizzle's index().on(...).where(sql`...`)); if db:check still reports a difference for an expression index, keep the SQL file as the source and follow what docs/ci-migrations.md says for rules Drizzle cannot express.
Add a case that reads pg_indexes for the eight names and expects each to exist with its predicate text containing 'business', 'invoice.failed' or 'waiting' as fits.

commits.title: The invoice job reads what is marked as waiting each tick, and keeps today's full check as an hourly net

changes.how: (1) Keep storesWithDocumentWork() (line 71) as the NET, with two changes: in its refunds branch add `and rf.created_at > now() - make_interval(days => ${LOOKBACK_DAYS})`, and put `order by store_id` before `limit ${limit}` so no store is starved when more than 50 have work. (2) Add `storesWithMarkedWork(limit = STORES_PER_RUN): Promise<string[]>`, the FAST path, one statement: `select store_id from (select e.store_id from commerce.order_events e where e.type = 'invoice.failed' and e.created_at > now() - make_interval(days => ${LOOKBACK_DAYS}) and not exists (select 1 from commerce.invoices i where i.store_id = e.store_id and i.order_id = e.order_id) union select d.store_id from commerce.order_edits d where d.status = 'applied' and d.documents = 'waiting') x order by store_id limit ${limit}`. (3) issueWaitingInvoices(storeId) today swallows a failure into 0: make it return `{ issued: number; failed: boolean }` (or add a sibling that does and keep the old name for its other callers; list them with rg -n 'issueWaitingInvoices\(' src). (4) invoiceJobs(options: { net?: boolean } = {}) (line 116): `const stores = options.net ? await storesWithDocumentWork() : await storesWithMarkedWork();`. In the loop call issueMissingCreditNotes(storeId) ONLY when issueWaitingInvoices reported failed (the SQL function issue_waiting_invoices() already ends with issue_missing_credit_notes(); today it runs twice per store). Everything else in invoiceJobs() stays in both modes: ensureSubscriptionEvents, reconcilePendingRefunds, sendPendingDocumentNotices, the try and the log. An order paid just now needs no job: its invoice is issued with the payment; the fast path only retries marked failures, and the net finds the rest within the hour.

In the registry of step 3.3 (JOBS): keep `invoices` at every 300 with `run: () => invoiceJobs()`. Add `invoiceNet: { every: 3600, why: "the full check for a paid order or refund with no document, which the marked path cannot see; an hour is the longest an unmarked invoice waits", work: { perStore: { cap: 50, order: "store_id" } }, budgetMs: 20000, run: () => invoiceJobs({ net: true }) }`.

A try at once where the cause goes away. Find where the seller's details and the invoice settings are saved: rg -ln 'invoice_settings' src/server -g '!*.test.ts' and, for the seller's details, the writer the Waiting tab's message points to (docs/wave-1b-invoices.md 2.1 names it). If the save function is not in this file, edit the file it is in and name it in the commit message. After a successful save, call `after(() => issueWaitingInvoices(storeId))` (after from "next/server"; outside a request, as in tests, call it directly behind a try). Nothing else in the save changes.

Existing cases must pass; where one calls invoiceJobs() and expects an invoice that waited for the seller's details to be issued by the job, pass { net: true } (that is the net's work) and change nothing else. Add: 'a failed invoice (an invoice.failed event) is retried on the next tick through the fast path'; 'completing the seller's details issues the waiting invoice at once'; 'one tick calls issue_missing_credit_notes once per store' (statement counter); and the plan's case: seed one store with 2,000 paid, invoiced consumer orders (insert in batches of 500 with the file's helpers), `select pg_stat_force_next_flush()`, read seq_tup_read + idx_tup_fetch of commerce.orders and commerce.invoices from pg_stat_user_tables, run one invoiceJobs() (fast), one sendPendingDocumentNotices() and one runEinvoiceSending(), flush and read again: each table rose by fewer than 100.
